column1: # vitrum packages — one row per logical package.
#   logical   name used in this file and in messages
#   portage   Gentoo atom, or - if Gentoo does not package it
#   pacman    Arch package, aur:<name> for the AUR, or - if Arch does not package it
#             Both columns accept "a|b" (installed if either is; the first is installed)
#             and a trailing "@cmd" (counts as installed when that command exists).
#   need      required, or the optional component that wants it
#             (nvidia, sddm, plymouth, live-wallpaper, phone, tmux, games, utilities,
#             cli-tools, file-manager, ocr, ocr-ru, nvim; lib/components.sh)
#   keywords  portage only: keyword written to package.accept_keywords/vitrum, or -
#   use       portage only: USE flags written to package.use/vitrum, or -
#   env       portage only: "half" builds with half the jobs (package.env/vitrum), or -
#   dnf       Fedora package, copr:<owner>/<project>:<name> for a COPR,
#             rpmfusion:<name> for RPM Fusion free, or - if Fedora does not package it
#   xbps      Void package, or - if Void does not package it
#             Every package column accepts "a|b" and "@cmd" as above, and "." for
#             "not needed here" (the distribution has it in another package, or
#             as part of its base): skipped without a word, where "-" — really
#             not packaged — is noted. The dnf and xbps columns come last so
#             that the older columns keep their numbers.
# A row that is - for one distribution and that lib/assets.tsv names (its last
# column) is fetched from upstream there instead.
# Gentoo atoms were checked against gentoo, guru, gentoo-zh and hyproverlay on 2026-10-01;
# Fedora 44 and Void (glibc) names in containers on 2026-10-21.
# Fedora and Void split headers into -devel packages, and Fedora has no base-devel:
# these rows are what niri's build needs there; Arch and Gentoo have it already (.).
# Fedora ships the pulse server, pactl and pw-play apart from PipeWire itself.
# runit starts nothing by itself: Void needs the system bus and elogind (login1,
# XDG_RUNTIME_DIR) as services, and a cron daemon for plocate's daily update.
# The password store apps keep their secrets in (Secret Service), unlocked at login.
# Settings → Displays: one screen mirrored on another (niri has no mirroring of its own).
# ocr: text from screenshots. English always; Russian (ocr-ru) when the
# Fedora's sddm wants a greeter display server; this one is Wayland (weston), not Xorg.
# games: game mode and its HUD.
# utilities: the microphone noise filter, the visualiser, a mixer, archives,
# phone: KDE Connect (pulls a good part of KDE Frameworks).
